description: Implement production-ready security enhancements: replace in-memory rate limiter with persistent solution or document limitations, add environment variable validation for all secrets, implement database connection pooling configuration, add error boundary for client-side errors, improve CSP with nonce-based inline script allowance (if feasible with Next.js 15), add security.txt and rate limit API routes.
steps: 1. Rate limiter enhancement: Add clear warnings in lib/rate-limit.ts comments and docs/SECURITY.md that in-memory limiter is per-instance only. Add redis-based alternative implementation in lib/rate-limit-redis.ts (conditional on REDIS_URL) following same interface. Update auth actions to use Redis limiter when configured.

2. Environment validation: Extend lib/env.ts to validate all required secrets (AUTH_SECRET min 32 chars, CRON_SECRET min 24 chars when used, EXOTEL_WEBHOOK_SECRET min 24 chars when telephony enabled). Add startup check that fails fast if production environment is misconfigured.

3. Database connection pooling: Add explicit connection pool configuration in lib/db.ts for production. Document recommended pool size in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md. Add connection_limit and pool_timeout to DATABASE_URL guidance in .env.example.

4. Error boundaries: Create app/error.tsx (root error boundary) and app/(app)/error.tsx (authenticated section boundary) following Next.js 14/15 conventions. Log errors server-side without exposing stack traces to client. Already exists: app/(admin)/dashboard/error.tsx.

5. Improve CSP: Research Next.js 15 nonce support for inline scripts. If supported, update next.config.mjs to use nonce-based CSP removing 'unsafe-inline' for scripts. Document the tradeoff in docs/SECURITY.md if not feasible.
6. Add security.txt: Create public/.well-known/security.txt following RFC 9116 with contact email, policy URL, and preferred languages. Add to public/ directory.

7. API route rate limiting: Add rate limit middleware wrapper in lib/api.ts that API routes can opt into. Apply to sensitive routes: /api/leads/import, /api/leads/export, /api/reports/*/export, /api/auth/me (lower limit than login).

8. Add monitoring helpers: Create lib/metrics.ts with functions to export prometheus-style metrics (if monitoring added later): db connection pool stats, rate limit hits, session counts. Make it optional/no-op if monitoring not configured.
9. Update docs/SECURITY.md with all new mitigations, remaining risks, and production checklist updates.
10. Update docs/PRODUCTION_CHECKLIST.md with new environment validation requirements and security configurations.
acceptance_criteria: Rate limiter includes Redis-based alternative that is used when REDIS_URL configured
Environment validation covers all security-critical variables with proper minimums
Database connection pool is explicitly configured for production use
Error boundaries catch and log client-side React errors without exposing internals
CSP is improved where feasible with Next.js constraints documented
Sensitive API routes have rate limiting applied
Documentation reflects all new security measures and tradeoffs
verification: Startup with missing AUTH_SECRET or misconfigured secrets should fail with clear error
Verify /.well-known/security.txt is served in dev server: npm run dev && curl http://localhost:3000/.well-known/security.txt
Check that error boundaries exist: ls app/error.tsx app/(app)/error.tsx
findings: Current state: lib/rate-limit.ts is in-memory Map, loses data on restart, separate counts per instance (documented in SECURITY.md as caveat #1). lib/env.ts validates only DATABASE_URL, NODE_ENV, APP_URL, AUTH_SECRET (min 32). Missing validation for CRON_SECRET, webhook secrets. lib/db.ts uses default PrismaClient with no explicit pool config. No root error boundary (only dashboard has one). CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' scripts (documented caveat #2). No security.txt. API routes have no rate limiting (only login/password-reset in actions have it). Monitoring/metrics not implemented.
